name: Slovakia

facts.religion: Catholic about 56%, Lutheran about 5%, no religion about 24%

snapshot: Robert Fico's government dismantled the anti-corruption prosecutor, softened the criminal code and targeted NGOs, drawing large protests and EU concern.
culture: Slovakia's castles, wooden churches and the High Tatras mountains are national treasures. Folk traditions, including the fujara shepherd's flute, are UNESCO-listed. Ice hockey is the biggest sport. Slovaks and Czechs understand each other's languages and remain close since their peaceful 1993 split.
society: Slovakia makes more cars per head than any other country, with plants for Volkswagen, Kia, Stellantis and Jaguar Land Rover. Fico survived an assassination attempt in 2024. His government has cut military aid to Ukraine and moved closer to Moscow, while large protests in Bratislava have opposed his course.
situation: In 2018 an investigative journalist, Ján Kuciak, and his fiancée were shot dead in their home while he was investigating links between politicians and organised crime. Mass protests forced Prime Minister Robert Fico to resign. He came back, won the 2023 election on a platform of ending military aid to Ukraine, and survived being shot five times by a lone gunman in 2024. Since then he has moved Slovakia toward Viktor Orbán's model, and in 2026 his allies in Europe got fewer.

Fico's government abolished the special prosecutor's office that handled high-level corruption, softened the criminal code in ways that let convicted fraudsters out early, and passed a law requiring NGOs with foreign funding to register, which critics called Russian-style. In 2026 parts of that agenda hit walls. Slovakia's Constitutional Court struck down the NGO law, and after the European Commission opened infringement proceedings in January, the coalition repealed a law dissolving the whistleblower protection office in March (CIVICUS Monitor). The European Parliament for the first time demanded proceedings to protect the EU budget from misuse in Slovakia, citing rural tourism subsidies diverted to luxury villas linked to Fico's associates (Daniel Freund MEP). In March Fico joined Orbán in refusing to back an EU loan for Ukraine. Then in April Orbán lost power in Hungary, leaving Fico as the EU's most Moscow-friendly leader. Tens of thousands have protested regularly since late 2024. The next election is due by 2027.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads a coalition with the confidence of the 150-seat National Council; the directly elected president has limited powers but can veto laws and appoint judges.
holders: Prime Minister Robert Fico (Smer), since October 2023; President Peter Pellegrini.

update.html: Fico's Smer-Hlas-SNS coalition lost its majority on 3 November when MP Roman Malatinec joined former environment minister Tomáš Taraba's new project, leaving it with 75 of 150 seats. On 11 November Taraba's three-member group voted with the opposition to sink a government amendment on benefits for cooperating defendants, which Fico had called a priority, 75 votes to 74 with one abstention. The opposition calls it a minority government and wants early elections, which Fico rejects.
